title: Slow Cooker Butter Chicken
description: A lighter butter chicken with cauliflower cooked into the sauce, finished with cream and Greek yoghurt.

items.name: mild chilli powder
items.prep: see notes; Australian chilli powder is much hotter

items.name: passata
items.prep: the source says "tomato sauce", which is US for passata, not ketchup

items.name: cream and milk, half each
items.prep: or full-fat coconut milk; not light, it waters down the sauce

method.title: Cook the aromatics
method.instruction: Heat the coconut oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion until it starts to soften, about 5 min. Add the ginger, garlic, curry powder, garam masala, chilli powder, salt and tomato paste and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

method.title: Load the slow cooker
method.instruction: Tip the onion mixture into a 6 L slow cooker. Lay the chicken on top, then the cauliflower, then pour over the passata. Nudge the florets and sauce around with a spoon so they're coated, leaving the chicken undisturbed underneath. Scatter the butter over the top.

method.title: Slow cook
method.instruction: Cover and cook on low for 4-6 hr (or high for 1½-2½ hr) until the chicken reaches 74°C. Check early; breast dries out if it goes too long. Lift the chicken onto a board to cool slightly.

method.title: Finish the cauliflower
method.instruction: Stir everything well to coat the florets, cover and cook on high until the cauliflower is completely tender. Skip this if it's already tender.

method.title: Shred and finish
method.instruction: Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and return it to the slow cooker. Stir in the cream and milk. Let it cool for a few minutes before stirring in the yoghurt; added too hot, it curdles. Serve over rice, quinoa or naan with coriander.

notes: Converted from a US recipe. American chilli powder is a mild spice blend; Australian chilli powder is straight ground chilli. Use a mild one, or swap in 1 tsp sweet paprika + ½ tsp ground cumin + a pinch of cayenne.
US "tomato sauce" is plain unseasoned tomato purée. Use passata, never ketchup-style tomato sauce.
The tomato paste was a 6-oz (170 g) can. A 140 g tub is close enough.
Chicken thighs would hold up better than breast over a long cook if you'd rather not watch the time.
Dairy-free: coconut oil for the butter, coconut milk for the cream, and a non-dairy yoghurt.
Keeps 5 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently.
